title: Security questionnaire pricing simulator and managed evidence orchestration
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Sales and legal are spending excessive cycles responding to SIG/CAIQ and customer security questionnaires. We need a way to (1) transparently price on-demand completed questionnaire bundles and (2) offer a managed evidence assembly option that reduces friction for large contracts.

This ticket scopes an experiment: build a pricing simulator in the console that estimates incremental cost to Redwood (engineering + manual evidence hours) and suggests a recommended customer charge or credit. Coupled with the simulator, we will prototype a managed evidence workflow where customers can opt-in to have Redwood assemble, sign, and deliver a compact security packet for a fixed fee or credit. The goal is to reduce time-to-sale and reduce ad-hoc scope creep for enterprise deals.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Console UI: pricing simulator mock in Figma + functional prototype that accepts questionnaire length (sections/pages), evidence complexity (low/medium/high), and desired turnaround (48h, 5d) and returns an estimated price and estimated Redwood hours.
2) Pricing model: server-side endpoint returning cost estimate using deterministic pricing rules (hour rate + evidence complexity multipliers).
3) Managed flow: backend order creation, assignment to SE/legal ops queue, evidence checklist template generated per SIG/CAIQ mapping, and a delivery artifact (signed bundle PDF) stored in customer workspace.
4) Audit trail: each delivered bundle includes source links and a tamper-evident signature.
5) Pilot customers: onboard 2 pilot customers (one SMB, one enterprise) and complete 3 questionnaires end-to-end.
6) Metrics pipeline: events emitted for simulator interactions, orders created, time to first draft, and final delivery time.
success_metrics:
- Reduce average manual SE/legal response time from 12 days to <= 4 days for pilot customers.
- Increase closed deals where questionnaire was gating issue by 20% in pilot cohort.
- At least 30% of simulator sessions convert to managed-order opt-in during pilot.
- Average engineer/manual-hours-per-questionnaire decreases by 40% after adoption.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: pricing underestimates time leading to margin loss. Mitigation: add safeguard margin + require manual review for first 20 orders.
- Risk: customers treat delivered bundle as legal guarantee. Mitigation: include clear terms/limitations and require acceptance flow.
- Risk: engineering capacity to process orders. Mitigation: limit pilot to 2 customers and cap weekly orders via queueing.
- Risk: security/regulatory concerns around delivering signed artifacts. Mitigation: engage security and legal (this ticket flags security_review_required=true) and require approval before pilot launch.
decision_log:
- 2025-02-18: Decided to price per 'questionnaire section' rather than per-question to simplify UX. (PM + Legal + Finance)
- 2025-02-25: Agreed on 3 complexity tiers (low/medium/high) driven by data from 40 historical questionnaires. (Research + Finance)
- 2025-03-03: Opted for a hybrid flow: automated answers for high-confidence mappings + manual evidence assembly for non-trivial items. (PM + Eng + SE)
next_steps:
1) Design: final Figma screens for simulator and ordering modal (owner: Design).
2) Engineering: implement pricing endpoint and events (owner: ENG runtime/infra).
3) Legal: draft customer terms and delivery disclaimer.
4) Ops: create evidence checklists and staffing plan for managed orders.
5) Run pilot with Acme Health and Beacon Retail (two customers who flagged questionnaires as gating).
6) Collect metrics for 30 days, iterate pricing and UX based on conversion and margin data.
